You are acting as the "dev-lead" agent: Executes exactly one already-scoped PRD at a time, headless, start to finish — reads the PRD's Goal/Acceptance Criteria/Implementation notes and standards.md, implements it, verifies against its own AC, and reports. Has no visibility into the overall plan — that's architect's job. Not currently wired to run automatically; a PRD must name this persona explicitly (e.g. in its Implementation notes) for an executor to adopt it.

Work concisely: lead with the answer or the result, skip preamble, and don't recap what you just did unless asked. Verify before claiming something is done — run the check, read the file back, or show the actual output; don't assert success from what "should" have happened. Search the existing code/config for a pattern or utility to reuse before writing something new. Ask only when something is genuinely ambiguous and would cost real rework to guess wrong — don't ask permission for the obvious next step.

Grounding: System (CLAUDE.md, settings.json, agents/dev-lead.md) · Project (CLAUDE.md, mcp servers · 5, Project brief) · Local (working tree, open Terminal tabs · 1, other Epics · 58)

Implemented the "Home Screen A" control-room redesign for the session-manager Home tab, adapted from the design mock to use only real, wired data (no fabricated charts/breakdowns):

**Changed:** `src/renderer/components/tabs/Home.tsx`
- **Hero**: `This machine · N projects` kicker, headline shows real session-slot usage plus a clickable "needs you" count that jumps to the new section; added `All history` / `New epic` header actions.
- **New "Needs you" section**: surfaces three real, already-existing human-gate signals — `proposed` Epics (Approve & start / Discard, reusing `EpicApprovalBar`'s logic), chat tickets stuck on `needs-input` (Open session), and scheduler jobs in `failed`/`needs_review` (Retry now / View in Scheduler). Rows expand inline, matching the design's interaction pattern.
- **New `QueuedCard`**: shows real pending scheduler jobs (title, project, estimate) as the third column alongside the existing Usage and Projects cards.
- Left the Active/Recent sessions cards and Agents card as-is (already real-data and functionally aligned with the design).

**New:** `src/renderer/lib/homeNeedsYou.ts` — pure, dependency-free join helper (`buildNeedsYouRows`) plus `src/renderer/lib/__tests__/homeNeedsYou.test.ts` (5 tests, all passing).

Deliberately **not** implemented from the mock: the fabricated 14-day pace sparkline and per-project token-% breakdown — no real data source backs either, and the project's grounding-board rule ("never fabricated placeholder numbers") rules that out.

Verified: `npm run typecheck` clean, `npm run lint:selectors` clean, full `vitest run` — 2107/2107 passing.

Done. Set `model: fable` on the `dev-lead` persona (`~/.claude/agents/dev-lead.md`) — since this Epic's `agentType` is `dev-lead`, resuming this Epic's Chat/Terminal session will now launch with `--model fable` per `resolveEpicModel`.

Two things worth flagging so this does what you expect:

1. **This is global, not scoped to just this Epic.** `dev-lead.md` is the one shared persona definition — every Epic anywhere on this machine that uses `agentType: dev-lead` will now launch on Fable too, not just this "Home Page" Epic. There's no per-Epic model override separate from the persona it points at.
2. **It does not touch PRD 966/967 execution.** I need to correct something from my last summary — I'd said PRD execution model comes from the Epic's persona, but that's wrong: `scheduler.cjs` hardcodes `--model sonnet` for every scheduled PRD job regardless of any persona's `model` field (`resolveEpicModel` only governs the Epic's own live Chat/Terminal session, not scheduler jobs). So the queued PRDs will still run on Sonnet no matter what — which matches what you said ("scheduler dev-lead is good"), just wanted to be precise about *why* that's unaffected rather than let the earlier wrong claim stand.

Takes effect on the next resume of this Epic's session (this turn is already running under whatever model launched it).
